info.title: Liberu Ecommerce — Multi-Tender Payments API
info.summary: Payment plans, admissions, an append-only tender ledger and outstanding balances.
info.description:
A fragment, meant to be merged into a host's document under the server prefix below.

Multi-Tender Payments owns the plan and the arithmetic. It never moves money and it never holds a balance. Three figures are therefore never accepted from a caller: **the payable total**, **the outstanding balance** and **a tender's capacity**. All three are resolved server-side through contracts the domain publishes, and no request body or header in this document names any of them.

A caller declares what it is *offering* — a tender kind and either an amount in minor units or a relative share. The module measures that offer against the total it resolved itself, refuses a plan that exceeds it, and partly spends a tender that falls short of what was asked of it.

servers.description: Default prefix. A host may re-prefix these routes through config('multi-tender-payments-api.prefix').

tags.name: Plans
tags.description: What an order costs and what it still owes. Both computed, never stored.

tags.name: Tenders
tags.description: The append-only ledger: admitting a plan, recording a tender, reversing one.

get.summary: Read a plan, its payable total and its outstanding balance
get.description:
The payable total is resolved through `ResolvesPayableTotal` on every call and the balance is a fold over the ledger. There is no status field: `satisfied` is the fold reaching zero.

The plan row is opened if it does not exist yet. It carries an order reference and a currency and nothing else — no status, no cached balance — so materialising it changes no answer.

get.summary: Page through a plan's append-only ledger
get.description:
Oldest first, ordered by id rather than by `occurred_at`: two entries can share a timestamp, and a page boundary that is not a total order silently drops or repeats a row.

A ledger entry's `idempotency_key` and `payload_hash` are never rendered.

post.summary: Append one tender to the ledger
post.description:
The plan is re-admitted against the total the host resolves *now*, and `position` names which admitted tender is being recorded. The module stores no pending plan, so a total that moved between admitting and recording is caught here rather than silently honoured.

`201` when the entry was appended; `200` when the idempotency key replayed one that already existed.

The two idempotency failures are opposite instructions and are separate classes in the domain, never one class separated by reading a message: `409` means the same key arrived with different facts and retrying will never help; `423` means the first attempt is still running and the identical retry will succeed, and it carries `Retry-After`.

There is no transaction across gateways. Record one tender at a time, as each institution answers. A decline recorded here leaves every earlier capture exactly where it was.

post.summary: Ask whether a plan is admissible, and what each tender would contribute

200.description: The plan is admissible. Nothing has been stored.

post.summary: Reverse a captured tender by appending a reversal that carries its reason
post.description:
The ledger has no update path and no delete path. A reversal is a **new** entry pointing at the one it reverses, because the capture it undoes happened at an institution this module does not control.

A reversal is **not** a refund. Deciding that money is owed back to a customer belongs to `ecommerce-refunds`, and nothing here creates anything there.

Idempotency is carried by the ledger: a tender can be reversed exactly once. Replaying the identical reversal returns the entry that exists (`200`); a second reversal under a different reason is a permanent conflict (`409`). The `Idempotency-Key` header is required all the same, so that every state-changing operation here has one contract.

example.reason: Gift card redemption failed at the issuer after capture.

apiToken.description:
A bearer token whose abilities are checked with `tokenCan()`. An actor that cannot answer `tokenCan()` is refused, not admitted — an unanswered authorisation question is an exposure.

Scopes are transport capabilities. This package makes no business authorisation decision about a plan; that belongs to the domain module.

scopes.ecommerce:multi-tender-payments:read: Read plans, balances and the tender ledger.
scopes.ecommerce:multi-tender-payments:write: Admit plans, record tenders and reverse them.

OrderReference.name: order
OrderReference.description: The host's opaque reference for the order. The module never interprets it and never looks anything up with it — it hands it to `ResolvesPayableTotal`.

TenderId.name: tender
TenderId.description: The ledger entry being reversed. It must belong to this plan; one that does not is a 404 rather than a cross-plan reversal.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Required on every state-changing operation, so that a repeat is a repeat rather than a second movement of money.

Mint it once, when the step is entered, and send the same value on every retry. A key minted at click time defeats the mechanism entirely.

On a `409` do **not** mint a fresh key: a fresh key on a conflict records a second tender for money that moved once.

Money.title: Money
Money.description:
Integer minor units, with a decimal presentation carried as a **string**.

`decimal` is a string and never a number: `19.99` in JSON is a double in every client, and `(int) (19.99 * 100)` is 1998. Nothing in this API returns a floating-point money value.

minor.description: The amount, in the currency's minor units.

currency.description: ISO 4217 alphabetic code. It has one origin: the payable total the host resolved.

exponent.description: Minor units per major unit, as a power of ten. Told to the module, never looked up.

decimal.description: The decimal presentation. A string, always.

TenderKind.title: TenderKind
TenderKind.description: No kind has a priority. Tenders apply in the order the caller declares.

TenderEffect.title: TenderEffect
TenderEffect.description: What the entry does to the balance: `captured` subtracts, `reversed` adds back, `declined` moves nothing. There is no "plan failed" effect.

PaymentPlan.title: PaymentPlan
PaymentPlan.description: No status field and no cached total. `satisfied` is the fold reaching zero.

Tender.title: Tender
Tender.description:
One entry in the append-only ledger, and simultaneously the allocation record: which tender covered which portion of which plan, in which declared position.

`idempotency_key` and `payload_hash` are deliberately absent.

position.description: The caller's declared order, recorded rather than inferred.

partly_spent.description: True when the tender contributed less than was asked of it. Partial satisfaction is the normal case, not the error case.

external_reference.description: Whatever the module that actually moved the money handed back.

instalment_reference.description: An external schedule identifier and nothing more. This module runs no scheduler and holds no due date as authoritative.

TenderWritten.title: TenderWritten
TenderWritten.description: The entry that was written, and what the plan owes now that it exists.

PlannedTender.title: PlannedTender
PlannedTender.description:
What a caller is **offering**, which is not one of the three figures this API refuses to accept. Declare an `amount_minor` or a `share`, never both.

There is no currency here: every amount is denominated in the currency of the payable total the host resolved, so a tender cannot disagree with its order.

amount_minor.description: What this tender is asked to contribute, in the order's minor units.

share.description: A relative weight. The payable total is split across the weights exactly, by largest remainder, with ties broken in declared order and no residue.

reference.description: Whatever the host's capacity resolver needs to identify this instrument — a gift card code, a store credit account. Never interpreted here, and never a balance.

position.description: Which admitted tender this call is recording.

effect.description: A reversal is not recorded here; it has its own operation.

external_reference.description: What the module that moved the money handed back.

reason.description: Required. A reversal without one is refused.

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description: Every refusal in this API has this shape. `code` is stable and is what a client branches on; the message is for a human.

errors.description: Field-keyed validation messages. Present only on a validation failure.

TenderWritten.description: The ledger entry, and the plan's balance after it.

error.message: This operation requires an authenticated actor.

MissingScope.description: The actor's token does not carry the scope this operation needs — or cannot answer `tokenCan()` at all, which is refused rather than admitted.

TenderNotFound.description: No such tender in this plan's ledger.

error.message: Tender [77] is not in the ledger of order [order-9f2c].

PermanentConflict.description:
A permanent conflict. Retrying will get the same answer forever, and minting a fresh idempotency key would record a second tender for money that moved once.

`idempotency_conflict` — the same key arrived with different facts.
`reversal_conflict` — the tender is already reversed under a different reason.
`tender_ledger_is_append_only` — something tried to edit or delete a recorded tender.

error.message: Idempotency key [5b0f2f4e] was already used for a different tender.

Unprocessable.description:
The request is well-formed but cannot be acted on.

`payable_total_unknown` — the resolver is bound and answered null for this order. A fact about the order, and **not** the 503 below.
`over_allocated_plan` — the tenders exceed the payable total. Refused, never clamped.
`mixed_currency_plan` — a currency or exponent disagrees with the order's.
`cannot_allocate` — the arithmetic has no exact answer.
`cannot_reverse_tender` — not captured, already reversed, or no reason given.
`idempotency_key_required` — a state-changing operation arrived without one.
`position_not_admitted` — no admitted tender at that position.
`tender_declaration_ambiguous` — a tender declared both an amount and a share.
`validation_failed` — see `error.errors`.

error.message: No payable total is known for order [order-9f2c].

ClaimInFlight.description: Transient. The same idempotency key is being processed right now, and the identical retry will succeed. Wait `Retry-After` seconds and send the **same** key.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait. Matches the ten-second TTL the domain takes its idempotency lock for.

error.message: Idempotency key [5b0f2f4e] is already being processed.

ResolverUnbound.description: The deployment has not bound a contract the domain publishes, so no money figure can be resolved. This is a deployment fault affecting every order — not a fact about this one — and it is deliberately a different status from the 422 above. A half-configured deployment can read nothing that needs a total and can record nothing that moves money, which is the correct failure direction.

error.message: The deployment has not bound [Liberu\Ecommerce\MultiTenderPayments\Contracts\ResolvesPayableTotal], so no money figure can be resolved.
